Consequently, the need for managing separate accounts across various social platforms will become obsolete. Web 3.0 imagines a forthcoming internet that prioritizes decentralization and democracy over the current model. In the future, services won’t be dependent on a single provider or a select group of providers; instead, algorithms will play a key role in hosting websites.

articleTitle: AI Based Weed Locating and Deweeding using Agri-Bot
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Farming, a fundamental aspect of human society, has evolved significantly over time. In the modern era, there’s a growing emphasis on natural products and reducing harmful chemicals to maintain soil and plant health, crucial for sustainable agriculture. This paper introduces an innovative approach to farming by integrating technology with agriculture. It presents the design of an AI-based Agri-Bot for detecting and eliminating weeds on farmlands without resorting to harmful chemicals. The Agri-Bot employs high-intensity lasers for precise weed termination, targeting only the weed tissue. The integration of software and hardware components is detailed, including image processing for weed identification. The bot’s design parameters, controllers, and hardware components are elaborated upon. Various components used in the Agri-Bot, including the Jetson Nano controller, Intel RealSense camera, Rhino motor, laser module, stepper motor, LIDAR, and more, are described in detail. These components work together to create a powerful and efficient Agri-Bot. Image processing plays a pivotal role in the Agri-Bot’s operation. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained using a dataset of farmland images to accurately identify weeds. The paper provides insights into the working of the Agri-Bot, outlining how it utilizes LIDAR for mapping, cameras for weed detection, and AI for decision-making.

articleTitle: PFCM Approach for Enhancing Classification of Colon Cancer Tumors using DNA Microarray Data
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Colon cancer stands as one of the most lethal diseases affecting the large intestine. While it primarily afflicts older adults, its occurrence is not constrained by age. Typically, it originates as benign cell growth within the colon, eventually progressing to cancer due to somatic alterations affecting gene expression. DNA microarray technology offers a standardized means of assessing the expression levels of numerous genes. This technology distinguishes tumors across various anatomical regions based on gene expression patterns. However, the sheer volume of microarray data presents challenges, particularly in dealing with the curse of dimensionality. In the first level, PFCM technique is employed to reduce the dimensionality of genes or features. To evaluate the effectiveness of these techniques, we applied four suitable classifiers as Non Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Bayesian LDC and Detrend Fluctuation Analysis. The classifier known as Detrend Fluctuation Analysis, which incorporates the PFCM Feature Extraction technique, achieves the highest level of accuracy, specifically 88.71%.

Author Keywords: Bayesian LDC and Detrend Fluctuation Analysis

articleTitle: Surface Treatment on Cellulose Fibres Produced from Natural Plants: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Increasing requirement for sustainable resources in a variety of applications, considerable attempts have been made to create lightweight, biodegradable, and renewable composites that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. They are all plant fibers and share certain characteristics, including the fact that they all produce highly nutritious seeds and have lengthy, durable fibers. Natural fibers reinforced with biopolymers obtained from either plant or animal sources have been recycled since ancient times to meet eco-friendly social needs such as clothing, handicrafts, composites, carrier bags, biodynamic agriculture, automotive, and textiles. Because of the extensive use of synthetic fibers, the use of natural fibers has declined substantially since the turn of the century. Natural Plant-based fibers include nettle, hemp, flax, cotton, coir, jute, kenaf, sisal, pineapple, banana, bamboo, etc. Natural plant fibers are mostly made of cellulose, which can be found in hillsides, former plantations, and wastelands. The fiber surface treatment (retting) process enhances the dissolution of the components that hold fibers together (primarily pectin, hemicelluloses, and lignin), which is a prerequisite for getting fibers suitable for use in the textile industry. Water, dew, chemical, and enzymatic retting procedures were used to remove natural fibers from raw materials. This paper proposes different categories of ecological surface treatment for natural fiber biodegradability, an approach aimed at promoting high-value-added natural products. The chemical retting method pollutes the environment and causes skin problems that affect human health, so we review the natural methods of surface treatment like fungi, bacteria, and enzymes.

articleTitle: Swarm Intelligence based Deep Learning Method for Health Monitoring System using Internet of Things (IoT)
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The research conducted is significant because there is an increasing demand for reliable health monitoring, particularly in underserved and far-flung areas. However, issues with data quality, network optimization, and resource limits might hinder the efficacy of data collected by IoT devices, which otherwise provide until then unimaginable prospects. Swarm intelligence and deep learning together can improve these areas, making IoT-based health monitoring more effective. Efficient sensor placement, data transmission, and processing of massive, frequently noisy health data streams are among the biggest obstacles to widespread adoption of IoT-based health monitoring. Using swarm intelligence algorithms to optimize sensor placement and deep learning for data analysis, the proposed Internet of Things-based swarm health monitoring system (IoT-SHMS) approach addresses the aforementioned challenges. IoT-SHMS uses swarm intelligence techniques, such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), to optimize sensor location and network topologies. This helps to increase the reliability of health prediction while decreasing operational expenses. Constant patient monitoring, early detection of health anomalies, and the detection of falls are a few of the numerous applications of an IoT-SHMS approach in the medical field. It additionally has applications in telemedicine, wellness monitoring, and emergency response systems to give doctors and nurses up-to-date information in a timely manner. Extensive simulation evaluations are presented to prove that IoT-SHMS works as intended. The advantage of our technology over conventional approaches is illustrated by the performance criteria of accuracy, latency, and energy efficiency. Based on these findings, IoT-SHMS appears to be a viable option for healthcare applications in the Internet of Things environment

articleTitle: AI Based Tamil Palm Leaf Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: An extensive study aimed at analyzing characters from old Tamil manuscripts written on palm leaves corresponds to Tamil Palm Leaf Character Recognition. These culturally and historically valuable manuscripts require extensive processing in order to effectively extract characters because they are frequently affected by chronological and degradation. The process begins with the capturing of a clear photograph of the manuscript, which is then preprocessed to remove imperfections like stains and smudges. Before preprocessing, the digitalized manuscripts are cropped vertically into three parts to improve the preprocessing quality. To remove color differences and compress the data, the image is converted to grayscale. subsequently noise is removed using specialized filtering algorithms. The image is refined through further morphological processes, which fill in small gaps and blurs character borders. Binarization makes it easier to distinguish the characters from the surroundings. Line segmentation is applied to the previously divided image to separate out individual lines of text for improved character recognition. Finally, the preprocessed scripts are trained by using CNN model. In the proposed model the Tamil characters are effectively recognized with an accuracy of 91%, and resulting in the digital preservation and comprehension of these precious palm leaf written works.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement-based Q-Learning Approach for Improving Energy Efficiency and Resource Management in V2X Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Recent advancements in technologies have paved the way for developing intelligent transportation systems that offer safety and autonomous services on the road through the utilization of Internet and cellular technologies. Vehicles equipped with sensors are capable of transmitting data to other vehicles or infrastructure, serving various types of services. Efficient radio resource management schemes have become more important due to the increase in the number of vehicles on the road, along with other wireless devices. This paper introduces an innovative method utilizing Deep Reinforcement Q-Learning to enhance Energy Efficiency and Resource Management within V2X communication networks, in conjunction with established mobile networks. Initially, the network congestion of the V2X framework such as vehicle positions, traffic conditions and available energy is defined for the representation of state information along with the existing mobile network. To optimize energy efficiency along with resource management we define the action space for varying the transmission power, selecting the number of vehicles along with their movement status and mode of communication. The reward function is initiated to provide incentivized actions that can reduce resource usage and provide optimization in energy consumption. The Q-Learning approach using a deep neural network (DNN) is implemented by selecting state as an input value and for every action provided in state information, the Q value in the output is updated. The results obtained from the numerical simulations demonstrate that the DRL-based Q-learning approach makes energy-efficient decisions and allocates resources efficiently by improving system throughput and avoiding collisions.

articleTitle: An Algorithmic Approach for the Detection and Classification of Lung Cancer from the Histopathological Images
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Lung cancer, a prevalent malignancy affecting both genders, demands early detection to mitigate its significant human toll. Unfortunately, symptoms often manifest in advanced stages, necessitating reliance on medical imaging for early diagnosis. Researchers have devised algorithms geared towards identifying lung cancer in histopathological images. This study introduces a computer-aided detection method using Flower Pollination Optimization for feature extraction from histopathological images. The study employs standard histopathological images sourced from the Kaggle database. In this investigation, five classifiers, including the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Non-Linear Regression (NLR), Naïve Bayes Classifier (NBC), Logistic Regression (LR), and Fisher Discriminant Classifier (FDC), are utilized to assess and categorize the Benign and Adenocarcinoma classes. Results show that the Naïve Bayes Classifier, combined with Flower Pollination, achieves the highest accuracy at 87.86%, according to established benchmark metrics.

articleTitle: Certain Examination on ECG Classification using Hybrid Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: A Non-stationary signal called an electrocardiogram (ECG) is utilized to evaluate the rate of cardiac beats. Doctors can identify Abstract - Heart Rate Variations (HRV) is one of the major issues focused in Medical field. The unexpected functionality of heart is measured from the Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. The HRV is one of severe disease which can affect any people of any age and it cause to sudden death. This research article focusses on identifying the HRV using the various Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. This research work develops the hybrid ML (HyML) which has better performance in all the aspects. The HyML is constructed with Support Vector Machine (SVM), Robust principal Component Analysis (RPCA) and Hidden Markov Models (HMM). Also, to support the different data of ECG multi SVM (MSVM) and Single SVM (SSVM) models were developed. These models are trained with 5348 samples under 8 different categories to classify the HRV. Therefore we propose the model HyML, which improvise the effectiveness on classifying the HRV. Our proposed model achieves the accuracy of 94.S3% for MSVM and 93.S9% for SSVM. The overall the sensitivity is varying between 0. S2-0.S9 for SSVM and 0.S2-0.9l for MSVM. Also, the precision observed in the range of 0. S7-0.91 for SSVM and 0.91 - 0.94 for MSVM. Hence, the proposed model is highly recommended model for HRV classification with SVM of both models such as single and multi.

articleTitle: Investigation on Indoor Detection and Tracking of People using IWR1642 mmWave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: There are several challenges associated with investigation in indoor detection and tracking of people using mm Wave sensors. One of the significant obstacle is the increased noise level and interference that can be present in indoor environments. Then it leads to false readings and false alarms. Advanced signal processing techniques such as beamforming and filtering are used. Another challenge is the need for a large number of sensors to cover the entire indoor area. This can be expensive and difficult to implement in practice. To address this, researchers are exploring to reduce the number of sensors required and they increased detection accuracy by employing cutting-edge algorithms and deep learning methods. Various applications such as home automation, advanced driver assistance system (ADAS), security, and healthcare that needs people count and detect the motion of people or object can use this advanced technology mmWave sensor. These mmWave sensors can provide better performance between the frequency ranges of 30 GHz to 300 GHz and can penetrate materials such as walls and clothing, making them suitable for indoor applications. The basic principle of indoor detection and tracking using mmWave sensors is by measuring the time taken by the radio waves to travel to the object from the transmitter antenna and reflected back to the receiver antenna. By analysing the reflected signals, it is possible to track and locate people in a particular specified area.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of a Renewable-Energy-Powered GSM Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The acquisition of driving skills is a crucial milestone in achieving autonomy for individuals with disabilities. However, the conventional driving system integrated into vehicles fails to offer the necessary features to enable those with impairments to operate the vehicle effectively. Therefore, the primary objective of this project was to develop a prototype of an automobile that operates using sustainable energy sources, specifically solar power. The target demographic for this vehicle is individuals who experience infirmities affecting their upper or lower extremities. The ability for those with physical limitations to independently commute between locations without relying on assistance would be highly advantageous. The research indicates that there is a growing focus on the topic of sustainable mobility among both the general public and experts. This is due to the significant influence of automotive systems on the production of carbon dioxide, climate change (namely global warming), and the depletion of fuel resources. The utilization of renewable energy sources, such as solar energy, offers numerous environmental benefits, including the reduction of pollution, the promotion of sustainability, and the absence of greenhouse gas emissions. This approach holds promise for safeguarding the environment in the long term. Undoubtedly, one of the most significant advancements in the realm of clinical practice that has greatly benefitted the elderly and individuals with disabilities is the introduction of portable mobility devices. The cost of an automobile may be deemed unaffordable for an individual of average means. In this particular instance, an effort is being undertaken to produce a Solar Electric vehicle designed for individuals with disabilities, with the aim of achieving an optimal cost and ensuring ease of use. The provision of accessible transportation and living arrangements guarantees that individuals with physical disabilities are able to experience comfort and ease in their travel and daily lives. Solar energy has emerged as a prominent focal point in contemporary times due to many factors such as environmental pollution, escalating fuel costs, and the limited supply of conventional energy sources. Solar energy is projected to become the predominant primary source in the future. The solar electric car incorporates sophisticated elements that prove highly beneficial for individuals with physical disabilities seeking to attain independence. Furthermore, the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) is affixed to the vehicle in order to facilitate the surveillance of those with disabilities. In the event of vehicle damage, loss of control, or any other unusual activities, it is necessary to transmit a notification to the designated individual through the utilization of GSM technology. The ability to remotely monitor individuals with disabilities from any location worldwide is advantageous.

articleTitle: Closed Loop Subspace Identification of a Real Time Non Square MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: When creating model-based control systems, the process model is extremely important. Here, uses a system identification method to create the process model. There are two different ways that this identification process develops: the open loop and closed loop approaches. We’ve set up a conical tank system on a laboratory scale using a non-square MIMO architecture as part of the project. Both with and without feedback techniques yield the system function for this conical tank system. We discuss the reasoning behind using these two methods. We use our laboratory-scale conical tank system to test the open loop system identification method, and we build a PI controller based on the knowledge we obtained from this process. We next use our conical tank system to implement the PI controller in real-time, and we record the data for closed-loop identification. We use a modified version of the N4SID algorithm to conduct the locked in kind of technique computation, which provides exceptional model achievement than the CVA method. The proposed / suggested improved N4SID identification technique is suitable for type of non square system matrix bsased MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Exploring Lightweight Encryption for Image Security using One-Dimensional Chaotic Maps
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The modern era has witnessed an unprecedented surge in image data generation and dissemination. This proliferation is not solely attributed to advancements in social media and e-commerce but is also significantly driven by the rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT). Several IoT applications, ranging from smart cities and remote surveillance to healthcare, rely significantly on visual information. Consequently, this emphasizes an urgent need for securing the sensitive and personal information embedded within the images. The conventional secure crypto primitives, primarily designed for textual and numerical data, often fail to provide robust and resource-efficient security measures for encrypting images. Contrarily, the highly random chaotic maps exhibiting considerable unpredictability are considered suitable for encrypting images. This paper explores the application of lightweight one-dimensional chaotic maps, including Logistic, Sine, Tent, and Chebyshev maps for encrypting the images. All the encryption schemes have been comprehensively evaluated in MATLAB in terms of several performance and security metrics, such as PSNR, MSE, NPCR, UACI, entropy, and execution time requirements. The findings in the paper highlight the potential of one-dimensional chaotic maps in offering balanced, computationally efficient, and optimal security solutions for safeguarding image data for diverse applications in the realm of IoT, multimedia, and beyond.

articleTitle: Respiratory Disorder Detection and Performance Analysis from PPG Signals using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Respiratory disorders pose a significant health concern, and their early detection is crucial for timely intervention and treatment. This paper presents a novel approach for the detection of respiratory disorders through the analysis of Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. We employ the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to extract essential spectral features from PPG signals, allowing us to monitor respiratory patterns and identify anomalies. The proposed method offers a non-invasive and cost-effective means of assessing respiratory health, making it suitable for widespread deployment. Furthermore, our work includes a comprehensive performance analysis of the STFT-based approach, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting respiratory disorders. The findings hold promise for improving healthcare by enabling early diagnosis and intervention in respiratory-related conditions. In the first level, STFT technique is employed to reduce the dimensionality of PPG signals. To evaluate the effectiveness of these techniques, five suitable classifiers as Principle Component Analysis, Logistic Regression, Gaussian Mixture Modeling, K Nearest Neighbor, Bayesian LDC applied. The classifier known as Bayesian LDC, which incorporates the STFT dimensionality reduction technique, achieves the highest level of accuracy as 78.05%, F1 score as 76.92 %, MCC as 0.56, error rate as 21.95%, Jaccard metrics as 62.50% and CSI as 53.95 %.

articleTitle: Certain Investigation of Various Algorithms to Improvise the Quality of Hearing Aid
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Hearing loss, marked by an inability to hear sounds below a 20 dB threshold, often results from dysfunction in the ear’s organs, associated nerves, or the auditory part of the brain. Deaf individuals encounter direct or indirect discrimination in daily life, as highlighted by National Centre for the Deaf data showing a significant employment gap. Only 48% of deaf individuals are employed, compared to 72% of their hearing counterparts. This discrimination leads to missed opportunities and some deaf individuals leaving jobs due to disability-related biases. After careful study of research papers done by scholars and working with low-end and High-end Hearing aid devices, we decide to start with the analysis of audio signals and implementing the different algorithms in computational tools like MATLAB and Python. Subsequently, we found the quality of hearing aid devices depends on three factors SNR, SI-SNR, and PESQ. Working with different algorithms and modifying some, we achieved better quality hearing aids than existing high-end hearing aids using the SepFormer algorithm. The overall systems shows better results on the signal quality improvements to ensure the HA perforamnce. The Metric GAN+based method has the good variations in SI-SNR of 9.42, PESQ of 3.15. Hence, using the proposed model enhance the quality of HA and supports the dumb people. The quality of the HA is analysed using this proposed mehtod with AI enabled technlogy.

articleTitle: Advanced Malware Analysis and Prevention
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Advanced malware poses a growing threat to the security of digital systems. This paper investigates the evolution of advanced malware, its stealthy characteristics, and the challenges it presents in contemporary cybersecurity. We analyse existing prevention strategies and propose an idea that leverages Python-based sandboxing, creating a virtual environment for malware analysis. This methodology aims to enhance the proactive detection and mitigation of advanced malware. Through empirical testing and case studies, the effectiveness of the sandboxing-based approach in thwarting emerging threats is analysed. This research contributes to the ongoing discourse on cybersecurity and offers practical insights for bolstering defences against evolving malware threats.

articleTitle: An In-Depth Survey on Environmental Sustainability: Mitigating Energy Footprints for an Advanced Future Outlook
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of interconnected devices leveraging a diverse array of sensors for internet connectivity, communally known as the Internet of Things (IoT), holds immense potential to reshape both the natural environment and the economic landscape. Despite the minimal individual energy requirements of each sensor, the cumulative power consumption of trillions of such devices is substantial. Consequently, prioritizing the development of long-term, energy-efficient solutions within the IoT framework becomes imperative. This article advocates for the adoption of environmentally conscious IoT technology, elucidating its stance through an exhaustive analysis of energy-saving perspectives and techniques within the IoT domain. The core focus is on fostering the creation of environmentally IoT solutions that are energy-efficient and sustainable. To achieve this overarching objective, attention is directed towards four pivotal components: Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communication, Water-Efficient Telecommunications, Eco-Sustainable and Power-Efficient Wireless Sensing Networks (WSN); RFID (Radio-Frequency Identity) systems with reduced energy consumption, and Power-Efficient Microprocessor Units and Integrated Circuits (IC).Through the incorporation of these foundational principles, this study aims to ensure that the economic and environmental ramifications of IoT remain positive and enduring in the years to come. The ultimate goal is to steer the trajectory of future generations towards the development and adoption of IoT solutions that are not only environmentally conscious but also economically viable.

articleTitle: Classification of Pavements into Bleeding and Non-Bleeding using Deep Architectures: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Bleeding or flushing refers to a reflective, dark layer of asphalt on the road caused by the upward movement of asphalt within the pavement. This issue is often caused by excess asphalt in the asphalt concrete, high temperatures, low air void content, and poor asphalt quality. The presence of bleeding poses safety risks as it creates an excessively smooth surface, lacking the necessary texture to prevent hydroplaning. This study presents a comparative analysis of various image classification models for the detection of bleeding and non-bleeding roads. The objective is to develop an automated system that accurately identifies road conditions related to bleeding, which is crucial for effective road maintenance and safety measures. In this regard, four pre-trained deep learning models such as VGG16, InceptionV3, EfficientNet, and ResNet50, to classify road images. The advantages of this work lie in the exploration of multiple state-of-the-art models, allowing for a comprehensive evaluation of their performance. The features and approach of the proposed work involve training the models on a labeled dataset of bleeding and non-bleeding road images. Each model is fine-tuned using transfer learning techniques, leveraging the pre-trained weights from large-scale image datasets. This study highlights several notable contributions about pre-trained deep learning models. In addition, the study identifies the strengths and weaknesses of each model, helping to guide future research and development efforts. The findings of this comparative study contribute to the field of road condition analysis and maintenance by providing valuable insights into the performance and limitations of different image classification models. The better performance is identified with InceptionV3 with an accuracy of 70.00% and least performance is given by ResNet50 with 31.66%.

articleTitle: EGFD-AROMA-based Pattern Forecasting with Crime Rate Level Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: In numerous cities, crime has become a chief concern that leads to the rising demand for timely predicting citywide crime occurrence. Therefore, this paper proposes an efficient forecast pattern with crime rate level identification. Primarily, the input crime video undergoes preprocessing. Afterward, the features are extracted. Then, by utilizing Permuted Congruential Generator-based Northern Goshawk Optimization (PCG-NGO), the important features are selected. Thereafter, feature similarities are identified. Conversely, the attributes are extracted from the crime detail dataset. Next, by considering the selected features, identified similarities, and extracted attributes, the crime categories are clustered using the JaroWrinkler distance-based K-Means Algorithm (JW-KMA). Then, the dependence strength is analyzed for the clustered categories. Lastly, for predicting patterns and crime rate levels, a Fuzzy Inference System and Convolutional Encoder Decoder-based Residual Neural Network (FIS-CEDRNN) is employed. By utilizing the extracted attributes from the crime detail dataset and the predicted patterns, Entropy Generalized Finite Difference-based Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (EGFD-ARIMA) is trained for forecasting crime patterns. The experimental outcome exhibited that the proposed technique withstands maximum accuracy when contrasted with existing methodologies.

Author Keywords: Permuted Congruential Generator based Northern Goshawk Optimization (PCG-NGO)
Entropy Generalized Finite Difference Based ARIMA (EGFD-ARIMA)
Fuzzy Inference System and Convolutional Encoder Decoder based Residual neural network (FIS-CEDRNN)

articleTitle: Ethics in Artificial Intelligence: An Analysis of Ethical Issues and Possible Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Unprecedented advances in Artificial Intelligence and its widespread applications in diverse fields without a sufficient social, ethical, legal, or technological framework to oversee it have sparked concerns about its decisions having ethical and social implications. Identifying and addressing the ethical issues of artificial intelligence has been a topic of great importance to researchers, governments, law enforcement agencies, and corporations, given the growing concerns of individuals, organizations, countries, and society. However, very little progress has been made to address them. These ethical and social issues, such as privacy breaches, bias, discrimination, non-accountability, less transparency, unemployment, promoting inequality, social manipulation, loss of human relationships, and independence, inevitably impact the existing social order and raise ethical concerns. This paper provides an overview and analysis of ethical issues, strategies for dealing with them, and techniques for assessing the ethics associated with artificial intelligence. Additionally, the study underscores the increasing ethical and social ramifications arising from the expanding use of technology in various domains. It also highlights insufficient technical solutions and a fitting framework to tackle these concerns. Ultimately, the paper emphasizes the necessity for thorough research to identify suitable technological solutions to address these ethical challenges.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Categorization of ECG Signal for Arrhythmia Detection with CNN - AlexNet
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Heart arrhythmia is indeed an irregular heartbeat caused by improper electrical signals in the heart. Some of these irregular heartbeats are harmless, while others can be very serious or even life-threatening. These irregular heartbeats can lead to symptoms that affect our ability to function properly. Arrhythmias are becoming more common worldwide due to modern lifestyles and dietary habits. China, India, Russia and the United States have seen maximum numbers of cardiac disease deaths. This emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis to prevent fatal outcomes. One common method of diagnosing arrhythmia is using an Electrocardiogram (ECG). However, the visual inspection or interactive analysis through ECG may not be very effective. To improve accuracy, efficiency, and speed in diagnosis, an enhanced methodology is proposed here. This includes using more appropriate parameters like the QRS complex and heartbeat rate, and combining them with a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) model. This combination could potentially provide better standards for detecting arrhythmias. By enhancing the detection process with these improvements, the approach could provide a valuable contribution to the medical field in detecting and diagnosing arrhythmias more effectively. This will potentially be a significant advancement in improving healthcare and preventing serious heart-related issues.

articleTitle: EEG Image Classification using Deep Metric Learning with Nearest Neighbor Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Many Deep Learning (DL) applications have been able to attain the best possible outcomes. The DL model is used for categorizing electrical brain signals for the interface between the brain and computer. Fast Fourier Transform converts time-domain Electroencephalogram (EEG) data to frequency-domain data. The Deep Metric Learning (DML) model using the nearest neighbor is used to train a spectrogram composed of 72 concatenated EEG channels. There were three sets of triplet pairings of epochs labeled positive, negative, and anchor in the training batch. The Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is combined with a triplet loss function for minimizing the Euclidean distance in embeddings of the identical class. RNN can also increase the distance among the embeddings of various labeled images to train an embedding feature. An EEG dataset of 22 untrained people was used to test the suggested approach. It was demonstrated that the DML method using the nearest neighbor can be used for training samples in a way that 100 EEG trials for a single subject. This model is used in the modification of the well-known problem of the substantial inter-individual inconsistency of human Motor-Imagery Brain-Computer Interfaces (MI-BCI) EEG with an accuracy of 0.75 percent.

articleTitle: Biomedical Interventions in Precision Medicine for Diabetics
publicationTitle: 2023 Third International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)
abstract: Precision medicine is the need of the hour strategy that deals with precision from diagnosis to treatment. There is a growing need for continuous monitoring of blood glucose levels and an effective algorithm to determine the right insulin dosages to achieve precision medicine for diabetes. This work intends to review the impact and importance of biomedical interventions in precision medicine for diabetes. It addresses the barriers that persist in practicing precision medicine for diabetes by strengthening the techniques of precision diagnosis and prognosis, precision therapeutics, precision treatments, and precision monitoring using predictive algorithms. The review emphasizes the significance of biomedical interventions in advancing the future directions of precision medicine for diabetes, including the integration of clinical trials with large datasets and continuous evaluation and monitoring of patients through regular measurements of blood glucose levels. By focusing on these biomedical interventions, this review aims to provide insights into the role of precision medicine in diabetes and its potential for improving patient outcomes.
